modal.title: Understanding RouteWard - Guide & Glossary
modal.subtitle: Plain-language explanations of the words used in RouteWard.

proxy.simple: An intermediary relay server. Websites see the proxy server's IP address and location instead of yours.
proxy.expert: L4/L7 transport tunnel supporting TCP relay, RFC 1928 UDP Associate, and HTTP CONNECT.

chain.simple: Routes your traffic through multiple proxies in a row for extra privacy, or automatically switches to a backup proxy if one goes down.
chain.expert: Sequential multi-hop tunneling (Entry -> Exit), high-availability failover, or automatic lowest-RTT node selection.

fake_ip.simple: Keeps your Internet provider from seeing which websites you look up, by using a temporary stand-in address for each website name.
fake_ip.expert: Bidirectional in-memory RFC 2544 allocator that intercepts DNS queries and recovers exact FQDNs on raw TCP/UDP socket connections.

killswitch.simple: A safety lock that immediately blocks an app's Internet access if the proxy disconnects, so your real IP is never exposed.
killswitch.expert: Strict DROP enforcement when the target upstream node fails or when UDP datagrams hit a TCP-only upstream proxy.

rules.simple: Your custom traffic laws: e.g., 'Firefox goes through Proxy', 'Steam connects Directly', and 'Windows Telemetry is Blocked'.
rules.expert: Deterministic ascending-priority evaluator matching process globs, domain wildcards, IPv4/IPv6 CIDR subnets, and port ranges.

system_proxy.term: Windows proxy setting or one app through the proxy
system_proxy.simple: 'System Proxy' configures all of Windows in 1 click. 'Run App via Proxy' launches a single chosen program inside the proxy tunnel.
system_proxy.expert: Toggles HKCU Internet Settings registry keys or spawns a child process with injected ALL_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY environment variables.

service.simple: A program that runs in the background, even when the RouteWard window is closed. It is what keeps your protection on.
service.expert: Windows service (or daemon) holding the interception engine, with a named-pipe IPC to the desktop shell.

port.simple: A number that goes after a proxy address, like a door number after a street address (for example 1080).
port.expert: TCP/UDP port (1-65535) of the upstream proxy listener or of the destination.

ip_address.simple: The address that websites see when you connect, a bit like a phone number. A proxy shows its own address instead of yours.
ip_address.expert: Public IPv4/IPv6 source address of outbound connections, replaced by the proxy exit address when routed.

protocol.simple: The "language" a proxy speaks (SOCKS5, HTTP...). Your proxy provider tells you which one to choose.
protocol.expert: Proxy handshake protocol: SOCKS4, SOCKS5 (RFC 1928, optional UDP Associate), HTTP CONNECT, HTTPS.

proxy_down.desc: Most of these problems come from the proxy, not from your rules. Test it first.

why.no_rule: No rule of yours applied: this is the default behavior.

alert.outage_body: Your Internet is cut on purpose so your real address stays hidden. Click here to open RouteWard, or use the RouteWard icon near the clock to pause protection for 15 min.
alert.outage_body_open: Your proxy is not answering, so some connections are failing. Click here to open RouteWard.

notice.title: RouteWard
notice.restored_body: RouteWard is not running, your normal connection was restored.
notice.exit_background_body: Protection continues in the background. To pause it, use the RouteWard icon near the clock. If your Internet stops working, open the Start menu and choose "RouteWard - Restore Internet".
notice.close_to_tray_body: RouteWard keeps running here, near the clock. Click the icon to open it again, or right-click it to exit.
notice.service_install_failed: Background protection could not be set up. RouteWard works for now, but protection will not come back after a restart.
notice.uac_cancelled: Permission was declined, so protection was not started.
notice.access_denied: RouteWard is running, but this account is not allowed to control it.
notice.start_failed: RouteWard could not start protection. Open RouteWard for details.
notice.toggle_failed: RouteWard could not change protection. Open RouteWard for details.
notice.pause_failed: RouteWard could not pause protection. Open RouteWard for details.
